[p0 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Fresh click-only puzzle. Probe 3 distinct objects: pink-center purple square (17,47), hollow ring (41,21), gray diamond (27,59) to learn click semantics on the chain nodes vs the disconnected ring.

[p1 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Probe empty far cell to determine anchor rule: does GrayDiamond stay fixed at (41,21) [predict Sq=(26,20)] or does old WhiteDiamond(27,59) become the new anchor [predict Sq=(19,39)]? Also tests whether empty cells are clickable at all.

[p2 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Test ring wants the SQUARE (pivot), not a diamond. Diamonds(3x3) docked in ring gave no reward; square is 5x5 (fills ring) with unique pink center. Click(49,21) moves WD right; click(41,21)=GD swaps anchor to (49,21); click(33,21) puts WD so Square=midpoint=(41,21) lands on the ring.

[p3 | acting_agent | action_plan]
L2 probe: click clearly-empty black cell (35,15) far from all nodes to see which node moves (the global white cursor?) and how the orange square recomputes, before committing to a square-onto-ring plan.

[p4 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Square=centroid(WD+grays) confirmed. Ring unreachable by WD alone, so grays must be movable. Probe: click orange grayB(49,9) to learn how a gray anchor relocates/swaps.

[p5 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Solve ORANGE: square=centroid of its 3 diamonds must hit orange ring(40,51), so positions sum to (120,153). Move WD->(31,43); select grayA(8,21) then move->(47,51); select gray(35,15) then move->(42,59). Final {(31,43),(47,51),(42,59)} avg=(40,51)=ring -> expect win.
